findings.title: Monitor context returns raw config instead of the prepared config copy
findings.body: get_monitor_environment_context() creates a copy of monitor.config and rewrites schedule_type to the human-readable display value, but then returns monitor_environment.monitor.config instead of the modified config variable. As a result, the monitor context attached to issue occurrences still contains the raw schedule_type value, and the display transformation is silently lost. The function should return the modified config object.

findings.title: Monitor status transition and incident creation are not atomic
findings.body: try_incident_threshold() saves MonitorEnvironment.status as ERROR before creating or fetching the MonitorIncident, and these operations are not wrapped in a transaction. If get_or_create fails or the process crashes after the status save, the monitor environment can remain in ERROR state without an active incident. Subsequent failed check-ins then take the ERROR branch, find active_incident=None, skip occurrence creation, and still return True, causing incidents/occurrences to be silently lost. The status change and incident creation should be made atomic or ordered so a failed incident-creation step cannot strand the monitor environment.

findings.title: Threshold check-in selection can be nondeterministic for identical timestamps
findings.body: When evaluating failure_issue_threshold > 1, previous check-ins are ordered only by -date_added before slicing. If multiple check-ins share the same date_added, the database may return them in an unspecified order. This can change which check-ins are included in the threshold window, which starting check-in is recorded on the incident, and what failure reason/evidence is generated. Adding a deterministic tie-breaker such as -id would make the selection stable.

findings.title: get_failure_reason() does not handle an empty status counter
findings.body: get_failure_reason() filters check-in statuses through HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP, but if no check-ins match, status_counts is empty. The code only special-cases a total count of 1, so it falls through to get_text_list([]) and produces a malformed message such as a leading-space ' check-ins detected'. Current callers generally pass failed statuses, but the helper is now in a shared module and should defensively handle an empty counter.
